intro: Families live all over the world. Some are big. Some are small. Some have grandparents at home. Every family has its own ways to help and care.
Homes are all over the world too. Some are tall city buildings. Some stand on poles by a river. Some are round and can move. Each home fits its weather and its land.
In this unit, you will meet families from many places. You will learn words like generation, custom, and shelter. You will tell about your own family and home.
bigQuestion: How are families and homes around the world alike, and how are they different?

timeline.t: Meet Rosa and her family at Sunday dinner in Chicago.
See that families come in many sizes.
Learn about cousins, aunts, and uncles.
Meet grandparents who live with grandchildren.
Find out how chores and customs help a family.
Help Bat's family move their ger in Mongolia.
Visit apartments, stilt houses, and adobe homes.
See snow-block shelters and snowy farmhouses.
Tell what every home needs and what makes it home.

words.d: a group of people who belong together and care for each other
the child of your aunt or uncle
a group of people in a family who are about the same age
a way of doing things that a family or group keeps for a long time
a job you do to help at home
something a family or group does again and again
a place that keeps you safe from wind, rain, cold, or sun
a brick made of mud and straw, dried in the sun

test.why: Families can be two people or many people. They come in many sizes.
Your aunt is your parent's sister.

test.q: Grandma, Dad, and you are how many generations?
test.why: Grandparents, parents, and children are three generations.
Picking up toys is a job that helps at home.

test.q: Mia's family eats pancakes every Saturday. That is a ___.
test.why: A custom is something a family does again and again.

choices: A round felt home that can move
test.why: A ger is a round home with felt walls. Herders in Mongolia take it when they move.

test.q: Which home keeps a family dry near a river?
test.why: Stilts hold the house above the water.
Adobe is a brick of mud and straw, dried in the sun.

test.q: Why does a Swiss farmhouse have a steep roof?
test.why: Lots of snow falls in the mountains. It slides off a steep roof.

choices: Shelter and a place to be cared for
test.why: Every home gives shelter. It is a place where people care for each other.

write.prompt: Pick two homes from this unit. How are they alike? How are they different? Tell or draw why each one fits its place.
tips: Name the two homes, like a ger and an apartment.
Say one way they are alike.
Say one way they are different.
Use a unit word, like shelter or weather.
